title: Source freshness registry
description: Schema for data/source_freshness.json — the PUBLISHED, reviewed statement of how current each tracked upstream source is. Freshness is a property of the SOURCE, not of a row: a row inherits it by reference, through the per-entry `source_freshness` marker in incident.schema.json, whose `sources` entries are keys into this file's `sources` object. This registry is the single place a newly-dead source is declared — flip its `status` to `stale` and set `last_success`/`stale_since`, and every row the source contributed to is marked on the next build with no schema change. Deliberately NOT the same artifact as ingest/_state/source_health.json: that file is the machine counter (high-churn, unreviewed by design, authoritative on the `refresh-state` branch per decision D5, and stale by design on `main`). This registry is a reviewed publication derived from it. The build MUST read this file and MUST NOT read the counter — reading the counter from a `main` checkout would ship D5's deliberately-stale copy as if it were current, which is a new instance of the exact class this registry exists to close.

_note.description: Free-text preamble for human readers of the raw file. Carries no machine meaning.

observed_at.description: Date of the source-health state snapshot this registry was last reconciled against — NOT the build date and NOT today. Deriving a freshness claim and stamping it with the build date is how a stale input becomes a falsely-current artifact; dating the artifact by its INPUT means an out-of-date registry reads as visibly old rather than as wrong.

observed_from.description: Which copy of ingest/_state/source_health.json the values below were reconciled against, named precisely enough to judge their strength: `main:ingest/_state/source_health.json` (stale by design per D5; the weaker provenance, and the only copy a build can read — so it is compared in full) vs `refresh-state:ingest/_state/source_health.json` (authoritative, and absent from a main checkout — so its values are reported NOT COMPARABLE here, never verified). Stated because the two can legitimately disagree and a reader must be able to tell which one they are holding. CLOSED VOCABULARY, on purpose: this is not free text. The enum mirrors `PROVENANCE_CONTEXTS` in scripts/validate.py, where each value's checking behaviour is enumerated with its reason, and tests/test_validate.py fails if the two drift. Free text made the escape hatch a one-line edit — any unrecognised value silently deleted the comparison and returned zero problems, so `checked and matched` and `not checked at all` were indistinguishable. An unrecognised value now fails twice: here on shape, and in the checker.
observed_from.$comment: Adding a legitimate context means editing three places in one PR: this enum, PROVENANCE_CONTEXTS in scripts/validate.py (with what the context means and what the checker does for it), and the Source freshness section of docs/DATA_DICTIONARY.md. Never widen this to a pattern or back to a bare string — the closed set IS the check.

coverage.description: What this registry does and does not speak for. Required, because a registry that lists four sources silently implies the corpus has four sources; naming the untracked ingests is what keeps that implication from being false.

tracked.description: Source keys this registry speaks for — the sources refreshed by .github/workflows/auto-refresh.yml and counted in ingest/_state/source_health.json. Must be exactly the key set of `sources`.

note.description: Plain statement of what is NOT covered, so absence from this registry is never read as a freshness claim.

sources.description: Registry keyed by source slug. The keys are the vocabulary the per-row `source_freshness.sources` array draws from, and are the same slugs ingest/_state/source_health.json uses, so the two can be reconciled key-for-key.

label.description: Human-readable name of the upstream source.

status.description: Refresh health, same three values scripts/check_source_health.py assigns: `ok` = last refresh succeeded; `degraded` = failed below the consecutive-failure threshold (a transient blip); `stale` = at or past the threshold, i.e. a source that has stopped working rather than hiccupped. Only `stale` propagates to rows — see `row_marker`. Retirement is NOT a status here: retiring a source is a corpus action (status + tombstone per Invariant 3), not a freshness value, which is why this enum does not need a fourth member for it.
status.$comment: This enum mirrors check_source_health.py's vocabulary on purpose. If that script's vocabulary ever changes, this enum and the reconciliation check change with it, in the same PR.

last_success.description: Date of the last refresh that succeeded. This is the AS-OF date for everything this source contributed: content it supplied is current through this date and no further.

stale_since.description: Date of the FIRST failed refresh after `last_success` — when the source actually broke, as distinct from when it crossed the failure threshold or when anyone noticed. Not derivable from the counter (which keeps only a tally and the latest attempt), so it is set from the run-log audit that established it and left alone. Omit rather than guess.

paused.description: True when CI alerting for this source is paused via ingest/_state/source_health.json's time-boxed override. Recorded here for the reader's benefit only: a pause silences the ALERT, never the freshness claim. A paused source that is stale still reads `status: stale` and still marks its rows, because the corpus must not describe itself differently depending on whether someone muted a notification.

hold.description: An open decision about this source's future, with the date it must be resolved by. Present when the structural question (retire / replace / restore / keep frozen) is deliberately deferred rather than unexamined. REQUIRED on every `stale` source (v2.13.0, user ruling D57; enforced below): a source that has stopped refreshing must carry a dated commitment to re-decide it, so that no stale source can sit in the registry undated. The dated form matters: the Phase-1 exit criterion for dead sources is satisfied by a remediation OR a hold WITH a decision date, so an undated hold must not be expressible as one. This is also the source's REVIEW DATE: `until` is what rows inherit as `source_freshness.review_by` (earliest `until` among a row's stale sources), so there is deliberately no separate `review_by` field here — one date, one meaning, one place (design note docs/audits/ws3-v2130-review-by-design-2026-10-09.md). When a hold's date passes, the hold is REPLACED by the decision that resolved or re-deferred it (a new `decision` id and `until`), with the lapsed hold recorded in the new `note`; a lapsed hold is never silently extended.

decision.description: Board decision id that opened the hold, e.g. D8.

until.description: Date the deferred decision becomes live, whatever else happens. Propagated to rows as `source_freshness.review_by`. DECLARATIVE: never compared with the wall clock by the build (the build path is deterministic); an overdue date is a matter for a scheduled check or a human, not for `make build`, so a lapsed `until` neither fails the build nor changes any row.

note.description: What is deferred and what would resolve it earlier.

row_marker.description: How rows this source contributed to are identified, so freshness can be inherited by reference instead of copied per row. Either a selector or an explicit null. `{"kind": "tag", "value": "<tag>"}` selects every entry carrying that tag — the tag each ingest script stamps on the rows it emits. `null` means this source deliberately does NOT propagate to rows, and `row_marker_note` must then say why (enrichment-only sources are the case: they add fields to rows other sources created, so marking the rows that happen to carry their data would point at the wrong set — the risk from their staleness is on the rows that DON'T).

kind.description: Selector kind. `tag` is the only kind, because every row-creating ingest stamps a source tag; a second kind should be added only when a row-creating source appears that does not, and never to paper over an enrichment source (use null for those).

value.description: The tag itself, exactly as the ingest script stamps it. Prefer the most specific tag the ingest emits (e.g. `aiaaic-sheet`, not the broader `aiaaic` that hand-curated rows also carry).

row_marker_note.description: Why this source does not propagate to rows. Required when `row_marker` is null.

note.description: Anything a consumer needs to interpret this source's freshness correctly — e.g. that a committed ingest snapshot keeps re-emitting the source's rows every build, which is why the corpus does not shrink when the source dies.

allOf.$comment: A null row_marker is a design decision, not an omission — it must say why.
v2.13.0 (user ruling D57): a stale source always carries a dated hold -- its review date. Remove this and an undated stale source validates again.
